title: Account → Connected apps
summary: Mara's Account page at Connected apps: one row per app she signs in to with Polaris Locker, saying how she signs in to it, when and on which device she last used it, and exactly what it gets, including what she declined (Diceroll gets neither her picture nor her email), with Change what <App> gets and Disconnect on each. Packages and Where you're signed in follow.
compare: 2026-10-20 shell (PX-35, BR-lockups): no header Activate (the account menu's first item); no footer (Help and Privacy are in the account menu); the docked Library · Discover phone bar with no Account tab and neither tab current (the account chip is the way in); the trimmed Locker lockup. The page frame follows the built Account (PX-31a): no email under the h1, the canonical section list with Packages in place of 'Access tokens', the section cards (kit .card.account-card), one column at every width (the 400 px aside at 1600 px is gone).
Build follow-up: Connected apps is not built (PORTAL.md §7: absent until its API exists; I-34, PX-31b). When built it sits between Sign-in methods and Packages, as drawn here and in portal.account.
The section list: Profile, Sign-in methods, Connected apps, Packages, Where you're signed in, Appearance, Your data; Connected apps is current. Sign out ends where the content column ends.
Each app row: the 40 px product icon, name and developer (from Presentation), then one line: the sign-in method it uses, when and on which device it was last used; then the chips of what it gets.

Granted items are chips with a tick; declined optional items are dashed, muted, unfilled chips with an eye-off icon worded 'Not your picture', 'Not your email'. Cloud Sync appears only for products that have it; a declined Cloud Sync reads 'Not Cloud Sync'.

'Change what <App> gets' (outline) re-runs the consent step for that app in the card, showing the current choices (identity.consent). 'Disconnect' (quiet danger text) confirms in the row (identity.disconnect).
Only products with Sign-in on appear. What Disconnect does is said once, in its confirmation. With no apps the card says: 'No apps yet. Apps you sign in to with Polaris Locker appear here.'
Packages and 'Where you're signed in' (browsers only, so browsers and apps are never mixed) follow in the build's order and anatomy (portal.account).

Phone: the section list is a pill strip, each app row stacks (icon and name, the method line, chips, then 'Change what <App> gets' and 'Disconnect' as full-width rows), and the docked bar sits below the content, never over it.

Portal v2 (B2, B12): the docked header, the one filled primary is ink, row actions outlined, the page h1 at the display step (48/52, 32/36 on a phone) with no full stop or eyebrow, no glow or wash; text never painted over art; weights 400/500/600.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Pass. Granted and declined chips differ by fill, Sign out lines up with the content, and phone buttons are full width.

findings.issue: Granted chips were outlined, not solid; 'Sign out' sat past the content column; on phone the tab bar covered Diceroll's buttons and they weren't full width; no empty state.
findings.resolution: Granted chips have a success-subtle fill and border; declined stay dashed and unfilled. The header is limited to the content column's width. On phone both buttons are full-width rows; the tab bar is drawn below the content (the renderer's phone rule) and Activate is the outlined .act pill. The empty state is specified in the compare, not drawn, declined: this story's Mara has two connected apps.

findings.issue: Destructive action weakest looking, buttons misaligned, lower half empty at wide.
findings.resolution: Row actions fixed width (Change 208px, Disconnect and Sign out one size); Disconnect is a quiet danger-text button; Sign out a bordered small button; 44px targets on phone; content capped and centred; 'Where you're signed in' in a side column at wide and its subtitle deleted; phone tab bar highlights Account (an Account tab added); chip scroller fades at its end.

findings.issue: Remove the privacy-id sentence from consent or connected-apps; move the device list into a tooltip.
findings.resolution: declined: the two screens are different moments and each must stand alone; tooltips are unavailable on touch.
